title: Release candidate 2 on paper, batch 3: pages 10 to 13, chapter 2, You are lucky to be here
how: Four photographs of pages 10 to 13 of the printed candidate, and one of the café table; notes 52 to 83, continuing the series. The handwriting was read by the journalist; two readings are uncertain and marked so.

first-page.name: The first pages sell the book
first-page.principle: The opening is about the reader, and the reason to read comes first (Zoom in, not discover).

show.name: Show the book, do not list it
show.principle: A story or a picture where an argument would do less.

altitude.name: Topics first, details under them
altitude.principle: Detail the point does not need is cut (Zoom in, not discover).

process-out.name: The making-of out of the reader's way
process-out.principle: The 2018 book and its outlines go to the section at the end.

voice.name: The voice is mine
voice.principle: Lines that sound odd, hedged or not like Dinis are rewritten.

reader-context.name: Meet the reader where they are
reader-context.principle: Explain a term before using it, with a short analogy, and say it first, then link.

evidence.name: Fact or opinion, visibly
evidence.principle: The reader can see which claims are backed by data and which are Dinis's opinion, and the data is found (Follow the rabbit holes).

links.name: The website holds what the page cannot
links.principle: Where the book needs more room, a QR code sends the reader to the site: the source, the explainer, the visualisation.

works.name: What works, keep it
works.principle: The ticks: what the pen approves is kept, and the format it likes is used again.

notes.means: The opening wonder ('I discover things I can do') should be about the reader, the ZX founder, not about Dinis.

notes.means: How to read this book should recommend this workflow: read on paper with a pen, photograph the pages, and let an agent capture the notes.
